{{Short description|Irish Carmelite priest, physicist and school teacher (1923–2008)}}

[[File:Synge Street Boys (7089812507).jpg|thumb|[[Synge Street CBS|Synge Street]] pupils, c.1941. Patrick (Thomas) Burke is pictured]]
'''Patrick Thomas Burke''' (1923 – 30 March 2008) was an Irish Carmelite priest, physicist and school teacher, and co-founder of the [[Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition|Young Scientist Exhibition]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.president.ie/en/news/article/bt-young-scientist-of-the-year-exhibition |title=Speech by President Michael D. Higgins at the 50th BT Young Scientist of the Year Exhibition RDS Dublin|website= www.president.ie|date= <!-- Wednesday -->8 January 2014}}</ref>

Burke was born 4 November 1923. He was educated in [[Synge Street CBS|Synge Street Christian Brothers School]] in Dublin. He joined the Carmelites, and studied in [[University College Dublin]], earning a Degree (1945), Masters (1947) and Doctorate (1949). He studied in [[Milltown Institute of Theology and Philosophy|Milltown Park]] earning a Theology degree and licentiate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.carmelites.ie/burkefuneral.html |title=Rev Patrick Thomas Burke|website= www.carmelites.ie}}</ref> Ordained in 1951, he also gained a Higher Diploma in Education in 1953.

Burke taught Mathematics and Physics at [[St. Patrick's College, Maynooth]], before teaching Mathematics at [[Terenure College]] in Dublin, where he also served as Prior and Headmaster. He joined the Physics department at UCD.

He co-founded with Dr [[Tony Scott (physicist)|Tony Scott]] his former pupil in [[Terenure College]] the [[Young Scientist and Technology Exhibition]] in 1965,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.btyoungscientist.ie/media-centre/exhibition-history|title=Young Scientist Exhibition History|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924234449/http://btyoungscientist.ie/media-centre/exhibition-history|archivedate=2014-09-24}}</ref> they came up with the idea while working in New Mexico in 1963. In 2007, they were awarded honorary doctorates by [[Dublin Institute of Technology]] in recognition of their promotion of science.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dit.ie/newsandevents/news/archive2007/first-2007-graduation-ceremony/ |title=Rev Dr Tom Burke and Dr Tony Scott conferred with Honorary Doctorates for inspiring thousands of young Irish scientists - 2007 |work=Graduation Dublin Institute of Technology}}</ref>

Burke died on 30 March 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/news/committed-educator-and-young-scientist-exhibition-founder-1.912673 |title=Committed Educator and Young Scientist Exhibition Founder |newspaper=The Irish Times|date=12 April 2008|accessdate=3 February 2022}} {{subscription required}}</ref>
